script.problem: It has 2 sentences. Explanations are 3 to 5 sentences.
A quote isn't the BSB's exact words.
It has 2 sentences. Explanations are 3 to 5 sentences.

terra.problem: Jonathan says he will stand beside Saul in the field, not that David will have company in his hiding place.
The explanation guesses why Jonathan chose this plan. His reason is not stated.
Jonathan says David has not sinned against Saul. Saying David did nothing wrong goes beyond that claim.
Being the king's servant does not establish that David was not an outsider. His identity as an Israelite is not established in this passage.
David does not stay right where he was. Jonathan brings him back to Saul after he has been hiding.
The passage says David was with Saul as before. It does not say they were in the same room or that everything was the same.
David being with Saul as before does not mean nothing has changed or establish that he is at the king's side.
The passage says the Philistines fled. It does not say the whole army turned around and ran.
The spear does not stay in Saul's hand. It strikes the wall when he tries to pin David with it.
The hair and garment alone are not what fill the bed. Michal also lays the household idol in it.
The text does not say Michal intended the figure to look asleep. She tells the messengers David is ill.
The text does not say Michal points the messengers at the bed.
The text does not specify which details David tells Samuel. It says he tells him all that Saul had done to him, not that he recounts the window escape.
The passage does not say the messengers never reached David or that they had no chance to seize him.
The passage does not say whether the messengers returned to Saul or stayed at Naioth.
Saul asks where Samuel and David are after he has already left for Ramah and reached Secu. The question is not where his journey started.
The text says Saul walked along prophesying, but it does not say he was not hurrying.
The passage does not say Saul was standing with the prophets. The saying follows his prophesying before Samuel and his collapse.
